description: We are Team Boca Juniors, enthusiastic students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Thrissur. We are passionate about space science, technology, and innovation. We aim to use NASA’s open data to develop creative solutions to real-world problems. We welcome motivated team members skilled in coding, data analysis, research, design, and presentation. Beginners eager to learn and collaborate are also welcome. Let’s innovate together!Team Name: Boca Juniors
summary:
Smart Earth Information Jukebox – Project Summary

What do we develop?

We propose to develop a Smart Earth Information Jukebox, an interactive web application or digital kiosk that converts real Earth data into music and sound. It uses information such as temperature, rainfall, ocean conditions and forest changes to generate different musical patterns.

How does it address the challenge?

The system transforms complex scientific data into simple audio and visual experiences. Users can select different environmental topics, listen to data-based sounds and explore related graphs and maps. It also provides an alternative way for visually impaired people to understand Earth information.

Why is it important?

This project promotes environmental awareness, improves accessibility and makes science education more engaging. By combining NASA Earth data, technology and sound, it helps people understand climate change and environmental conditions in an innovative way.

Our vision is to make people not only see how Earth changes but also hear its story.
details: Project Details – Smart Earth Information Jukebox (Earth Beats) Our project, Smart Earth Information Jukebox, is an interactive system that transforms Earth-related scientific data into sounds, music and visual information. It uses environmental data such as temperature, rainfall, ocean conditions and forest cover to create meaningful audio experiences. Users can select an environmental topic, explore graphs and maps, and listen to how different environmental conditions change over time. Benefits and Intended Impact: The project makes complex Earth science information easier to understand and more interesting. It promotes environmental awareness, supports science education and provides an alternative method of accessing information for visually impaired people. Our aim is to encourage people, especially students and young generations, to understand climate change and become more responsible towards protecting our planet. Tools and Technologies: We plan to use NASA Earth data sources for environmental information, Python for data processing, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the user interface, and Web Audio API for generating sounds. The system can operate as a web application or a touchscreen kiosk with speakers or headphones. Creativity and Team Considerations: The creative aspect of our project is converting scientific measurements into musical patterns using pitch, rhythm and sound intensity. Instead of only displaying numbers and graphs, we allow users to hear environmental changes. Our team considered data accuracy, accessibility, user-friendliness, affordability, technical feasibility and educational value while planning the project. We aim to make Earth information accessible, interactive and memorable for everyone.
